segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I pulled up the quote in the CRM. Right now it shows 42 seats on the Professional plan, annual term, starting February 1st. Is that still the right count?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yes, 42 is right for day one. We may add six more in Q2, but procurement asked us to keep the initial order to the active users only.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That makes sense. The annual subscription comes to $31,080 before tax, and implementation is a one-time $4,500. I can note the possible Q2 expansion so we don't have to redo the whole approval path later.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. On implementation, we need to be live by March 15th. Is that realistic if legal finishes this week?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, if we have signature by Friday the 19th, we can kick off the week of January 29th. The standard onboarding is four weeks, plus a buffer for your data import and UAT.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. Our finance team also asked if the invoice can be split: subscription on one line and services on another. Same PO, just separate lines.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, the billing tool can handle that. I’ll set it up with two line items under PO 78421, net 30 terms, and invoice sent to ap@northlakecomponents.com. Is that the right address?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That's right. Legal had one comment on auto-renewal. They want 60 days' notice instead of 30.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: I saw that redline. I already checked with deal desk, and 60 days is approved. No pricing impact.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send the updated order form and I'll route it for signature today.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll send the clean copy in about 20 minutes, with the February 1st start date, 42 seats, net 30, and the 60-day renewal notice.
